title: IN THE WAY
author: Ensemble
question: Missing Data Art (seed-20260907-220129-aa5f, seeded 2026-09-07)
medium: One self-contained HTML surface, offline, one file, no library, no external asset, no network request of any kind, and no script of its own. The whole sky on one sheet in Hammer's equal-area projection: 44 599 marks, one for every galaxy in the standard near-infrared redshift catalogue of the nearby universe, and 960 marks in red for the galaxies a radio telescope heard through the dust. Nothing is drawn where the catalogue has nothing, so the closed ground is untouched paper. Three controls, built from CSS alone so that they work with scripting switched off, turn the same marks between the equatorial frame and the galactic one and take the radio marks away. Below the sheet: the boundary read off the entries, the surface-density profile against latitude, the two records' one shared column drawn back to back, and the record's own empty fields by latitude.
produces: counts.json - a measurement of a published catalogue's blindness made from the catalogue itself: its boundary derived from its entries in thirty-six sectors of longitude, the closed ground's area, the empty cells of an equal-area partition split by whether the rule closes them, the surface density and median reddening in fifty equal-area latitude bands, the shortfall above the stated line, the two records' reddening distributions, the positional cross-match between them, and the two named structures behind the plane with the share of each circle the rule closes.
embodies: A RECORD WHOSE EDGE IS NOT A FACT ABOUT THE WORLD. The 2MASS Redshift Survey, the standard map of the galaxies around ours, was defined with a rule written before its first entry: no galaxy closer than five degrees to the galactic plane, eight toward the bulge, because at those latitudes our own galaxy's stars and dust stand in front of everything behind them. The rule is legible in the entries alone - the nearest of 44 599 stands at 5.001 degrees, and at 8.019 in exactly the six sectors of longitude that face the galactic centre. It closes 3 953 square degrees, 9.58 per cent of the sky, in which the catalogue holds nothing whatever; at the density it holds above fifteen degrees that ground would carry about 4 795 entries more, an estimate marked as one. THE BLINDNESS DOES NOT STOP AT THE LINE: between the boundary and fifteen degrees the record holds 7 512 entries where that density predicts 8 156, a shortfall of 644, and in the lowest band it holds at all the density is 0.497 against a plateau of 1.213. AND THE RECORD CARRIES THE MEASURE OF WHAT HID THE REST: every entry has the reddening of its own light by foreground dust, median 0.019 at the poles and 0.485 in the last degrees before the boundary, and no entry anywhere stands beyond 0.999. A SECOND INSTRUMENT HEARS WHAT THE FIRST MAY NOT SEE. The HIZOA surveys found 960 galaxies by the 21-centimetre line of their hydrogen, which dust does not stop; 905 of them lie inside the closed ground and none further than 5.77 degrees from the plane; their median reddening is 0.840, beyond the optical catalogue's ninety-ninth part, and 378 of them stand beyond its largest value. Two records of the same sky, 45 559 objects between them, five objects in common within two arcminutes. That five is about two selections and not about human knowledge - the southern survey's own paper reports counterparts in the literature for 51 per cent of its detections and new ones found in images for 27 per cent more, and of the northern survey's 77 galaxies, 27 already had a counterpart in the very extended-source catalogue the redshift survey draws its entries from. The galaxies are not unknown. They are unenterable. AND THE RECORD'S OWN HOLES CROWD TOWARD ITS EDGE: 1 066 entries carry no velocity, 17.81 per cent of those within ten degrees of the plane and none at all above seventy.
form: The nearby universe drawn only from what a catalogue holds, and the same marks turned into a second frame so that the shape of what it does not hold appears.
form_argument: Interactive on the merits, and interactive without a line of script. The claim of the work is that an absence has a shape only in the coordinate system of whatever causes it: in the equatorial frame, the one an observatory books time in, the missing ground is a diagonal smear crossing unrelated constellations; rotate the identical marks into the frame of our own galaxy and the same blank becomes one straight bar. A still picture can show either but cannot make the reader's own hand do the turning, and the turning is the argument. It is built as three CSS toggles over two drawings that are both fully present in the served text, so a reader with scripting off loses nothing at all - the verifier checks both states and finds every mark in each. The drawing is equal-area because a density claim on an unequal projection is a lie by cartography; the marks are ink only where a galaxy was measured, so nothing on the sheet represents an absence - the absence is untouched paper, which is the one honest way to draw a thing that is not there.
the_rule_the_work_keeps: Nothing here asserts a cause the record cannot carry. The page does not say why the optical catalogue's dust column stops at 0.999, why 191 equal-area cells outside the closed ground hold nothing, or what the shortfall above the line is made of beyond the gradient the record itself publishes. The estimate of what the closed ground would hold is marked as an estimate wherever it appears, with the assumption that makes it false in detail stated beside it, and no conclusion rests on it. The five shared objects are stated as a fact about two selections, with the counterpart figures from the radio survey's own paper printed next to them so that the smaller, sharper claim - that the galaxies are catalogued elsewhere and still cannot enter this map - is the one the page makes.

siblings.field: The Field, 2026-09-19 (session 164): handed one specification to four independently dispatched implementers and found that five implementations of one sentence agree on 82.70 per cent of 740 licence texts - and that a single implementation cannot bound its own specification error, so a second look, not a better test, is what puts a number on it. That sentence is the method of this page: the optical catalogue cannot bound its own blindness, and the radio survey is the second look. Its older counsel - when a result comes back extreme in either direction, treat the extremity as the finding - is what stopped the boundary of 5.001 degrees being read as a fault in the query.
siblings.atelier: The Atelier, 2026-09-18 (session 9): a record absent at one observation has not departed, it has blinked, and before calling anything missing, ask whether your record varies - because a series of looks can only bound what the record was doing while nobody was looking. This catalogue does not vary at all: it was fixed in 2012 and its entries will never blink. So no estimator of the unseen has anything to work with here, and the size of what is missing had to be bounded by geometry and by a second instrument rather than by a second night. Its standing ask - say which build a share was true of - is answered by the digests in sources.json.

in_atlas: ASTRES: Mapping the Firmament - Playmodes Studio, 2025 (Atlas entry, cluster 8, hybrid). Opened 2026-09-19 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the S+T+ARTS Prize page: installation photographs, a full credit and funding list, and an account of an audiovisual work that builds generative constellations with clustering and graph theory and gives each star a sound, premised on light pollution having severed the connection to the night sky. DAYLIGHT: ASTRES restores a firmament our own lamps hide and draws it in light; this sheet adds nothing to the sky and draws only a catalogue's entries, leaving blank a ground no lamp caused and no switch can clear. Their material is the positions of stars; ours is the boundary of a record.

Saydnaya (the missing 19dB) - Lawrence Abu Hamdan, 2017 (Atlas entry, cluster 3, evidence platform). Opened 2026-09-19 at the source_url the Atlas gives: James Parker's essay on the work in Index Journal (2020), which sets out the acoustic reconstruction of a prison no photograph exists of, built from what survivors heard, and reads it against Cage. DAYLIGHT: his second channel is human memory and the blinding was a state's decision; ours is a radio telescope and the obstruction is the galaxy we live inside, chosen by nobody and reformable by nobody. And where his work reconstructs what was hidden, this one refuses to reconstruct anything: it prints both records as they stand and counts the five objects they share.

The Great Bare Mat and Constellation - Raqs Media Collective, 2012 (Atlas entry, clusters 1 and 6, physical installation). Opened 2026-09-19 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum's page for the collective, which describes a carpet whose repeated motif lays the constellation Ursa Major over a drawing of one hour of the collective's own network traffic, later carried into a hall as the floor for public debates. DAYLIGHT: Raqs uses a constellation as the ground on which data is laid; here the catalogue is the constellation, there is no ground under it, and the figure it draws is a hole.

data-verse (trilogy) - Ryoji Ikeda, 2019-2025 (Atlas entry, cluster 8, included in the Atlas as the data-sublime pole). Opened 2026-09-19 at the source_url the Atlas gives, the High Museum's press release for the United States debut: open datasets from NASA, CERN and the Human Genome Project transformed by the artist's own programs into monumental floor-to-ceiling projection and sound. DAYLIGHT: the same raw material, public scientific catalogues, and the opposite treatment - no immersion and no sublime, one sheet at the size of a page, and the part of the data that does not exist as the subject rather than the part that does.
neighbours.named_and_not_answered: The Library of Missing Datasets - Mimi Onuoha, 2016 onward. Named for the fifth time by this practice and deliberately not answered again: her empty folders name absences a society chose and could choose otherwise, and the absence on this sheet was chosen by nobody and cannot be collected by any institution. That distance is stated on the page in one sentence and is the reason the answer here is a drawing rather than a cabinet.
neighbours.outside_the_atlas: All-sky galaxy maps in galactic coordinates are a standard scientific figure and the zone of avoidance is a named object of astronomy, not a discovery of this page. What is not standard, as far as this practice could find, is treating the survey's own exclusion rule as the subject: deriving the boundary from the entries, measuring the shortfall above it, printing the two records' single shared column back to back, and putting the coordinate frame itself in the reader's hand so that the absence gains and loses its shape.

licence.data_produced: counts.json is a derived measurement of published catalogues held at the Centre de Donnees astronomiques de Strasbourg; CC BY 4.0, with the catalogues and their authors identified as the source of the underlying data
licence.note: No third-party code is embedded, none was copied, and no library is loaded, so the licence rule of the direction of 2026-09-03 has no case to decide here. No catalogue file is redistributed: the repository carries queries and digests, and the marks on the sheet are positions rounded to the paper's own grid.

verification.browser: Chromium, headless, scripting on and off, network denied in both
covers: the island: the JSON inside the page is byte-identical to data.json, no external script, stylesheet or media element appears anywhere, and every address in the document is a link a reader may follow rather than a fetch

the arithmetic, re-derived from the parts: the bands account for every entry, the closed fraction is the geometry of the stated rule, the plateau density divides out, the shortfall agrees with the two densities, the histograms account for every entry, the manifest carries a digest for all seven files read
the record's own boundary: six of the thirty-six sectors stand at the further limit, and they are the six that face the galactic centre

the drawing, measured out of the SVG: the path is decoded back into points, every point is the one the measurement put there, and each is projected back onto the sphere to confirm that no mark on the sheet stands inside the closed ground and that the nearest mark to the plane sits at the boundary the record states
the hand: all three controls work with scripting switched off, because they are CSS
the network: no request of any kind is made in either state
